title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Pressure cleaning (all heights)
audience: Pressure cleaning owners and team leads who want repeat bookings and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer for pressure cleaning with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the client has checked the surfaces
instruction.body: Ask for a review or referral after the client has walked the driveway or path and agreed the result, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step, such as a review or the name of one neighbour who might want the same clean, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and the answer. One experiment (Baylor Keller Center, June 2024, not a pressure cleaning study) found that a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one: 2.16 per cent against 1.32 per cent of customers. Sending a review link or QR code is allowed, and Google provides one. Do not write reviews for clients or invent them. Do not screen out unhappy clients: asking only happy clients is called review gating, which Podium (a vendor) says Google treats as a violation. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says, and Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews.

instruction.heading: Offer the next clean before the client leaves
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose the next clean with a date: a driveway or path clean on a set interval, or a house exterior clean ahead of a visit the client has planned. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm the client agrees before you change their schedule. No source in this research gives a typical repeat interval for pressure cleaning, so choose one, record it as a test, and review the result. If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase.

instruction.heading: Check in at an interval you can test
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after the interval you have chosen. The check asks whether the surfaces still look clean, whether anything has changed, and whether there is other work to quote, such as a deck or a fence. Keep it short, record the reply and close the loop. A check that only asks about the result may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be, even when it is framed as a reminder. ACMA's summary does not say whether one-to-one messages are covered, so check that point before you send.

instruction.heading: Common-area clients need the plan first
instruction.body: Consumer Victoria says an owners corporation manages common property, and lists driveways, pathways, walls, stairwells and gardens as examples. That makes common areas a possible client route, but whether a particular surface is common property depends on the plan of subdivision. The research found no evidence of how often owners corporations buy pressure cleaning, and no real-estate or commercial property manager evidence. Re-contact committees only with a written offer and a clear opt-out, and do not plan a campaign around demand that has not been shown.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next clean or a small thank-you, and write down the payment condition, normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Give the referrer a copy, keep a record of each referral and whether the reward was paid, and never promise a reward you cannot deliver. Research on referral programmes (Xu, Yu and Tu, 2023) found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals in seven studies, so say the reward in the invitation. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so the tax and contract effect of a credit is unconfirmed; check it with an adviser.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-clean offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in at an interval you have chosen as a test, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each dated need in your own records, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A pressure cleaner finishes the driveway and front path for a regular client. She says she will recommend him to her neighbour in the same street, and he wants to offer her a credit on her next clean if the neighbour books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the neighbour books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes down the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the neighbour completes a paid job, and when the credit will be applied. He asks his client to pass on the neighbour's details, and he contacts the neighbour only if the neighbour agrees. He does not promise a reward he has not written down. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of the credit, he confirms it with an adviser. He does not agree to clean the neighbour's solar panels with a pressure unit, and he takes the job only if his licence and insurance cover it.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-clean offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of dated re-contact points from the business's own records
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the surfaces are right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo of their property or review without their consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are personal information. The OAIC's guidelines do not settle small-business coverage here, so check it for your turnover.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC's guidance says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder. ACMA has been enforcing this area, so check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. No licence for pressure cleaning was found in this research. Check the rule in each state where the work is done, and note that solar panels must not be pressure washed (Solar Victoria). This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-clean offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-clean offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the surfaces, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next clean in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a pressure cleaning client for a review or referral?
options: Before the job starts, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the surfaces are right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of the cleaned driveway at their home. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next clean for the client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

sourceReferences: Google Help, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: review links or QR codes may be shared; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on review content.

Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment, not a pressure cleaning study.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; Google's position not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer reward in the invitation. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022. Supports: the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: factual service reminders can be commercial.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown. Supports: unsubscribe honoured within five working days; inferred consent is narrow. The Spam Act 2003 text was not read.

Consumer Victoria, 'What is an owners corporation?', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/owners-corporations/buying-into-an-owners-corporation/what-is-an-owners-corporation, updated 9 April 2026. Supports: common property examples; subject to the plan.
Solar Victoria, 'Maintenance guide', https://www.solar.vic.gov.au/maintenance-guide, updated 17 July 2026. Supports: do not use a pressure hose on panels.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law. Cited for the height point; the Victorian rule was not checked.

WorkSafe Victoria, news release on falls risks in the solar sector, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-08/crackdown-falls-risks-solar-sector, 26 August 2026. Supports: allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Aimed at solar; the principle is stated for any roof.

Note: tax and contract effect of referral rewards are UNCONFIRMED. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found. No pressure-cleaning repeat interval or real-estate or commercial property manager evidence was found.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Taken from the CP-04 research file: commercial messages need the recipient's consent; each message must identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must have an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
